name: Tin telluride
equilibrium_context: Polar semiconductor; in the low-temperature rhombohedrally distorted phase topologically TRIVIAL due to inversion breaking; no Dirac cone in equilibrium

driven_states.emergent_property: Transiently appearing Dirac cone in the band gap - the first direct spectroscopic evidence of a Floquet TOPOLOGICAL state. Simultaneously, renormalization of the conduction band dispersion through hybridisation with Floquet sidebands. Proposed mechanism: light-driven band inversion with a change of orbital character.

drive.polarization: linear s and p, identical result

driven_states.source: Chassot et al., Nature Physics 22, 1282 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03341-0
driven_states.caveat: The claim of a topological state is considerably stronger than the measurement: what is observed is a transient Dirac cone plus band renormalization; the topological character is an interpretation supported by DFT, not by the measurement of a topological observable. Absolute field and fluence values are missing. Publication only in June 2026, no time for reproduction. The distinction from a Volkov state via the polarization null test is clean.

threshold.quantity: no field threshold, but a sharp resonance condition at the band gap - no effect at 1.55 eV

sources: Chassot et al., Nature Physics 22, 1282 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03341-0
gaps: Field and fluence values not in the main text.

provenance.notes: Literature search and field extraction by AI agents under the direction of D. Leonforte; every numerical value and citation checked against the cited work and every DOI verified. Not reviewed by a domain expert. Corrections are welcome and are the intended path to improvement.
